items.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022
items.q: I wrote introducing Archie Schepp article and he gave me some records to review

ctx.x: The poetry, did it lead somehow to writing record reviews and, or were your record reviews a way to make some income?

Yeah definitely. Let me see, Baraka got me into writing record reviews. He was doing it. And when I moved to New York he was my closest friend and he thought I could do it well and he introduced me to Dan Morgenstern who was the editor of not Down— Metronome magazine at the time, and Dan let me write some — I wrote introducing Archie Schepp article and he gave me some records to review, and so that’s how I got started in it. I wasn’t feeling all that qualified to do it to tell you the truth, but then when…

do it because all these articles were coming out about anti-jazz and John Coltrane was considered to be anti-jazz as was Cecil and numerous others, Ornette and others. And so I would go to this concert, and I would go to this one at the Village Gate say, and I’d hear John Coltrane, he’d be wailing. And I’d leave there really feeling like I just had the soul rinsing that I had mentioned in those liner notes that you referred to, and just practically limp from the experience, and I’d open the magazine and see that…
